name: Master build gate

# Run on the proposed PR merge commit, not just the topic branch. Keep this
# workflow unfiltered so its required check is always reported for master PRs.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [master]
  push:
    branches: [master]
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  master-build:
    name: master-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    env:
      NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=6144
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund

      - name: Test people date-hint normalization
        run: npm run people:hints:self-test

      - name: Test unresolved people-date holds
        run: node scripts/test-people-unresolved-hold.mjs

      - name: Test Cursor date-worker recovery
        run: node --test scripts/test-people-date-worker.mjs scripts/test-people-date-send-recovery.mjs scripts/test-people-date-workflow.mjs scripts/test-people-date-ownership.mjs scripts/test-people-date-preflight-diagnostics.mjs

      - name: Install ebook publication verification tools
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libxml2-utils imagemagick zip unzip

      - name: Test certified ebook people provenance and publication gates
        run: node --test scripts/test-people-identity-seal.mjs scripts/test-ebook-certified-people.mjs scripts/test-ebook-certified-cli.mjs scripts/test-ebook-people-readiness.mjs scripts/test-ebook-current-date-audits.mjs scripts/test-people-date-audit.mjs scripts/test-people-editorial-rejections.mjs

      - name: Test bounded canonical-person dossiers and chapter proofs
        run: |
          node --test scripts/test-people-identity-dossiers.mjs scripts/test-people-identity-dossier-store.mjs scripts/test-people-chapter-identity.mjs scripts/test-people-progress-ui.mjs
          npm run people:catalog:self-test

      - name: Test certified website people publication
        run: node --test scripts/test-people-qualified-site.mjs scripts/test-people-site.mjs

      - name: Build and validate the full site
        run: npm run build

# AGENTS.md

## Completion-first orchestration

Follow `PEOPLE_COMPLETION_PROCESS.md` before scheduling glossary work. It supersedes
old extraction-wave quotas and minimum extraction-batch sizes for identity work.
First prove a live nonempty chapter (continue the existing Jinshu 053 owner/work).
Pin source/editorial/date inputs and independently review each chapter person against
the accepted canonical dossier. Use bounded indexed retrieval; never generate a
complete same-name pair graph or require exhaustive negative comparisons. Preserve
reviewed cross-chapter uncertainty explicitly; hold concrete attribution or false-merge
contradictions. Reconcile changed evidence without recursively completing the corpus.
No new broad extraction wave until this path is proven; preserve/drain existing
claims. Do not weaken identity, chronology or publication gates. Report zero-person
reviews, data-qualified chapters and live published nonempty chapters separately.
A passing build or empty extraction is not the nonempty acceptance test.


## Repair English omissions when found

A definite English omission or mistranslation requires a concrete complete replacement,
not only a flag or an outside-scope note. Check both English fields and repeated uses.
Supply supplemental repairs in an artifact with book, chapter, unit ID, field, exact
before/after text and source-based reason; keep them separate from closed-schema date
or identity reports. The host routes these into the active editorial application work,
with a separate reviewer for worker-authored repairs. Preserve independent review and
normal extraction, chronology, identity, CI and publication gates. Do not defer known
fixable English to a future corpus-wide pass. An empty proposal queue alone does not
prove every source proposition has been translated.

## Host resource safety

Follow the crash-recovery operating profile in `PEOPLE_COMPLETION_PROCESS.md`.
`npm run people:disk:check` warns at 4 GiB macOS swap and rejects swap at 8 GiB,
combined Codex backend RSS at 4 GiB, or warning/critical memory pressure. At the
swap warning, inspect memory consumers and swap growth before increasing concurrency. These are conservative
dispatch stops, not OS guarantees. Check before each dispatch/local heavy job and
at least every 60 seconds while observing active work; a startup check alone is
insufficient. Do not launch more work after a failed measurement or failed guard.
Preserve live jobs, claims, locks and recovery; do not kill unrelated apps or delete
swap/history. A fresh chat must use a compact handoff, not a fork of the oversized
campaign conversation. Initially use no parallel native Codex subagents and only
one cloud assignment; increase remote concurrency only after measured safe runs.

## Local disk conservation

Before any local batch or workspace change, run `npm run people:disk:check`.
This read-only preflight fails below 30 GiB free or when a registered secondary
checkout contains `public/`. Workers share the host checkout and unique artifact
paths. Never copy the corpus, repository history, public assets, dependencies, or
ignored recovery state into a job directory. Preserve existing work and ownership.

The default chapter-worker topology is one shared host checkout plus isolated job
artifact directories, not one worktree per chapter. Workers read sealed packets and
write only their assigned artifact; the orchestrator performs validation and canonical
publication. Workers sharing a checkout must not independently switch branches, pull,
stage, commit, or build: those operations share one Git index and must be host-owned.
Use separate reviewer conversations for independence. Create a secondary sparse
checkout only when a task genuinely needs concurrent source-code editing or a different
revision. Do not clone or create a worktree merely to read evidence or produce JSON.
For a reusable clean secondary checkout, preview
`node scripts/prepare-people-sparse-checkout.mjs --checkout ABSOLUTE_PATH --book BOOK --chapter NNN`
and add `--apply` after checking process ownership. This exact-chapter selection omits
unrelated chapter files as well as site assets. The helper refuses dirty checkouts.

Follow `LOCAL_DISK_STRATEGY.md`. Keep one full checkout for global builds; local
chapter workers use reusable sparse checkouts without `public/`. Before creating
another checkout, check available disk and reuse an idle one. Below 30 GiB free,
stop new checkouts/full builds and reclaim verified completed work first. Archive
completed managed worktrees promptly after checking service/process dependencies and
preserving needed ignored recovery state. Do not create unmanaged `/tmp` worktrees
per chapter or review round. Independent reviewers require separate conversations
and sealed evidence, not full repository copies.

## Cursor Cloud specific instructions

This is a static-first site with one Cloudflare Pages Function for person records (no framework, no database). All scripts are vanilla Node.js ES modules requiring Node v22+.

### Key commands

- **Install deps:** `npm install` (includes `cheerio`, `satori`, `react`, `@resvg/resvg-js` for OG share images)
- **Build/rebuild site:** `make update BOOK=<book>` — runs citations, counts, manifest (merge), progress (merge), static HTML, **`scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs`** (`public/sitemap.xml` + `public/robots.txt`), **Open Graph PNGs** (`generate-og-images.js` with **`--incremental` by default**: skips when `*.png.sha256` matches the current source fingerprint), and sync for that book only. Use `make update-all` for every book under `data/`. To **re-raster every OG card** after layout/font changes, run with **`OG_FULL=1`** (e.g. `make update-all OG_FULL=1`), or bump **`OG_LAYOUT_VERSION`** in `scripts/og-fingerprint.mjs`. **`make backfill-og-sidecars`** writes only sidecars next to existing PNGs (no raster). People records are pre-rendered into 1,024 JSON shards and served at `/people/<slug>.html` by `functions/people/[slug].js`; a second sharded person-ID index permanently redirects URLs retired by merges or slug changes. Use `npm run people:site`, `npm run people:site:verify`, and `npx wrangler pages dev public` when working on them. **`public/data/search-corpus/`**, **`public/data/people/`**, and **`public/people/`** are gitignored build output; do not commit them in chapter PRs.
- **Cloudflare Pages:** In the project **Settings → Builds**, set **Build command** to **`npm run build`** (cannot be empty). **Build output directory:** **`public`**. Git-connected Pages does **not** read a build command from `wrangler.toml`—only the dashboard (or API) sets that. An empty build command skips the whole pipeline and deploys committed `public/` as-is (no manifest/HTML/OG regeneration). The deploy build intentionally does **not** run LanguageTool, because Cloudflare does not have the local LanguageTool server; update cleanup scores locally with `make update BOOK=<book>`, `make update-all`, or `make score-languagetool` before committing when scores matter. **`public/og/**/*.png` and `*.png.sha256` are tracked in Git** so clones and deploys include share cards; incremental builds still skip raster work when fingerprints match. The build ends with `scripts/verify-og-assets.mjs` (PNG validity + fingerprint checks). **`public/sitemap.xml`** lists chapter and hub URLs for crawlers; **`public/robots.txt`** references it via **`Sitemap:`**. After a deploy, spot-check `curl -sI https://<site>/og/site.png` returns **`Content-Type: image/png`**; HTML there usually means a missing file or rewrite rule.
- **OG images:** First run downloads Noto Serif CJK OTF into `fonts/.cache/` (gitignored). Override with `OG_FONT_PATH` + `OG_FONT_FAMILY`. Canonical URLs use `SITE_URL` (default `https://24histories.com`) in `generate-static-pages.js` and `generate-og-images.js`. Speed on CI: **`OG_CHAPTER_CONCURRENCY`** (max 16) and **`STATIC_GEN_CONCURRENCY`** (max 32) parallelize chapter OG and HTML; when unset, both scripts pick a default from **`os.availableParallelism()`** (see `scripts/build-parallelism.mjs`) and log it—override in Pages if you want a fixed cap. **`OG_BOOK_RESVG_CHUNK`** (default 16) batches book-hub SVG→PNG in fewer child processes (`scripts/og-resvg-batch.mjs`).
- **Validate JSON:** `make validate` (requires `jq`)
- **Serve locally:** `cd public && python3 -m http.server 8000`
- **View stats:** `make stats`
- See `make help` and the README for full command reference.

### Translation workflow

The standard translation loop is: `make start-translation BOOK=<book>` → fill in translations → `make submit-translations` (or `make continue`). See `prompt.txt` and README for full details.

- **Economical model choice:** The bulk of chapters consist of formulaic annalistic military records ("In year X, General Y attacked Z"). A less expensive model handles these well. Reserve a more capable model for famous rhetorical passages (speeches, debates, Sima Qian's commentary) where literary quality matters most.
- **TRANSLATOR and MODEL metadata:** Always use `TRANSLATOR="Garrett M. Petersen (2026)"` and set `MODEL` to the actual model name you are running as (e.g. `MODEL="Opus 4.6"`). Do **not** use your agent identity (e.g. "Cursor Agent") as the translator — the translator is always **Garrett M. Petersen**.
- **Article validator:** The `submit-translations.js` validator warns (non-blocking) when idiomatic translations lack English articles (`the`/`a`/`an`). These are informational only and do not block submission.
- **FILE= parameter:** Always use `FILE=translations/current_translation_shiji.json` (or the appropriate book name) with `make submit-translations` to avoid ambiguity if multiple translation files exist.
- **Batch size:** `start-translation` extracts 100 sentences per batch by default. For a 244-sentence chapter, expect ~3 batches. Commit every 4 batches per the workflow convention.
- **Score-translations length mismatches:** The quality scorer flags "length mismatch" for short classical Chinese sentences with longer English translations. These are false positives inherent to translating terse classical Chinese and can be ignored.
- **SDK translation failures:** `npm run sdk-inspect:run -- --from-log /tmp/sdk-translate-cloud.log` (or `--agent bc-… --run run-…`) prints agent URL, result summary, and last conversation turns. The orchestrator logs the same diagnostics on `status=error` automatically.
- **SDK editorial review:** `npm run sdk-review:list` shows the queue; `npm run sdk-review:cloud -- --book <id>` runs the next unreviewed chapter via `prompt-review.txt` (semantic fidelity, dialogue attribution, `make apply-review`). Optional `--until-complete` loops within that book or globally. **Batch:** `npm run sdk-review:batch -- --book shiji [--limit N] [--dry-run]` (or `sdk-review:shiji-batch`) launches parallel cloud review agents — independent of translation batch; default concurrency **10** (`SDK_REVIEW_BATCH_CONCURRENCY`); log `/tmp/sdk-review-batch.log`.

### Gotchas

- **Current parallel date runner:** The tested runner supports two concurrent
  chapters using one shared four-job pool across chapters. Keep stable workers,
  reservations, locks, leases, recovery artifacts, invocation ceilings and all
  independent review/publication gates. Do not reapply the historical
  `patches/date-audit-parallel.patch` to the current runner; it has already been
  adopted. `DATE_AUDIT_PARALLEL_HANDOFF.md` and that patch remain provenance.
  Adopt future runtime changes only after the current host invocation exits.
- **Independent people date audits:** Follow `PEOPLE_DATE_AUDIT.md` in every lane.
  All 4,099 chapters started date-un-audited; retain extraction prompt 7 and do not
  re-extract them for dates. After extraction and repairs, build a
  `people:dates:packet`, use a separate source reviewer, and record their complete
  report with `people:dates:record`. Capture acceptance is not date approval.
  Catalog completion, progress and ebook-glossary gates require approval. Run
  `people:dates:verify` before milestone builds. Preserve failed audits and research
  holds instead of guessing dates; `westernBounds` supports one-sided chronology.
  An unresolved reason saves extraction work but cannot pass the audit. Source or
  extraction edits make prior approvals stale. Do not launch a paid audit wave
  without calibrating size/cost and assigning unique resumable review ownership.
  `people:dates:run` now executes the audit/repair/fresh-re-audit loop. Cursor
  requires explicit `--run --model`; Grok Bot uses `--lane grokbot` attachment
  handoffs without SDK calls. Both reserve `dateAudits` in the shared queue,
  retain conversations and staged rounds, and publish only after independent
  approval. Managed days include dates between editorial and identity work.
  Oversized evidence fails before spending; inspect it instead of truncating.
  Run `people:dates:workflow:self-test` and the date-worker offline tests before
  changing recovery or publication behavior. Never count a failed/staged repair
  or a scheduled calibration target as an accepted chapter.

- **SDK translation orchestrator:** Per book, session *N+1* starts only after the previous chapter is on `origin/master` (merge-wait); books do not block each other (`--concurrency`). Local: `npm run sdk-translate:local -- --all-untranslated --concurrency 4 --until-complete` (direct push). Cloud: `npm run sdk-translate:cloud -- --all-untranslated --concurrency 19 --until-complete` (PR loop). **One chapter per agent (parallel, no merge-wait):** `npm run sdk-translate:cloud -- --book jinshi --chapter 068` — fan out many processes; each opens a PR but **does not** merge to `master` individually.
- **Translation PR batching (Cloudflare builds):** Workflow `automerge-cursor.yml` only labels `cursor/*` PRs (`translation-batch`); it does **not** auto-merge to `master`. `npm run merge-translation:staging` (or workflow **Merge translation PRs to staging**) retargets each open chapter PR to `translation-staging` and **merges it via GitHub** so chapter PRs show as merged; then **one** squash PR `translation-staging` → `master` (one ~10m build). `npm run merge-translation:staging:dry-run` lists queued PRs. `--git-only` keeps the old absorb-via-local-git behavior without closing PRs on GitHub. Staging merge conflict resolution keeps **chapter** files from the PR but **drops** `public/data/search-corpus/` from git (gitignored); a post-batch corpus rebuild runs locally only (not committed).
- **In-flight chapters:** `npm run translation-inflight` lists chapters reserved by open `cursor/*` PRs, work on `translation-staging` not yet on `master`, and local SDK claims (`data/translation-inflight.json`, gitignored). `sdk-translate --chapter` and `make start-translation` skip/blocked duplicates automatically when `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` is set.
- **Finish staging batch:** `npm run finish-translation-staging` closes absorbed chapter PRs, git-merges conflicted heads into `translation-staging`, and squash-merges the open `translation-staging` → `master` batch PR (requires `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`).
- **Shortest-chapter cloud batch:** `npm run sdk-translate:shortest-batch` (or `--dry-run`) scans `origin/master` for incomplete chapters, skips in-flight via `translation-inflight`, launches the 100 shortest with `SDK_CHAPTER_BATCH_CONCURRENCY` (default 25). Plan: `data/shortest-untranslated-batch-plan.json`; log: `/tmp/sdk-shortest-100.log`.
- **SDK drain:** `npm run sdk-translate:drain` / `npm run sdk-translate:drain-status`.
- **DeepSeek calibration:** `npm run people:deepseek:pilot` is an isolated,
  resumable benchmark for already-extracted chapters, not a production lane.
  Further paid trials are paused for economics; obtain explicit authorization
  before spending more, including on a calibration cohort. Preserve existing
  evidence and use the offline self-tests while paused.
  Use `--agent --max-units 60 --max-turns 300 --review --review-rounds 5`
  plus `--require-whole-chapter` for full-chapter calibration;
  `--run` authorizes paid requests within the existing shared $10
  ceiling. Completion requires the production validator plus full, focused
  chronology, and focused editorial approvals of the current draft. Never count
  partial chunks or a general-review approval alone as chapter completion.
  Preserve all ignored pilot responses, draft state, citations, and interrupted
  review reasoning. Do not publish these artifacts or bypass the shared queue.
  See `DEEPSEEK_PEOPLE_PILOT.md` and `npm run people:deepseek:self-test`.
- **People extraction lanes:** `npm run people:extract` and Grok Bot share the atomic
  ledger on `codex/people-work-queue`. Sync ignored local recovery state with
  `npm run people:queue:sync-cursor`; inspect it with `npm run people:queue:status`.
  Grok Bot must claim through `npm run people:grokbot:claim -- --worker <stable-id>`
  and must not call the Cursor SDK. Its extraction PRs target
  `codex/people-glossary-staging-v2`. All Grok assignments and all resumable Cursor
  conversations/chunks are sticky until completed or explicitly released. Grok workers
  must use the documented shallow sparse clone because the full history is roughly
  10 GiB and `public/` is unnecessary for extraction. When the GitHub connector does
  not authenticate terminal Git, the trusted orchestrator publishes the exact claim,
  the worker reconstructs it with `npm run people:grokbot:resume`, and returns the
  assembled file as a direct attachment. The orchestrator verifies its byte count and
  hash, saves it at the exact extraction path, then runs `npm run people:grokbot:accept`.
  See
  `GROKBOT_PEOPLE_LANE.md`.
- **Local Grok Build extraction:** Follow `GROK_BUILD_PEOPLE_LANE.md`. It is a
  separate subscription-backed `grok-build` queue lane, not Grok Bot or Cursor.
  Use a stable worker ID, dry-run one explicit chapter, then use `--run` only
  after checking its queue ownership and allowance. Its direct proxy transport
  supplies bounded read/write/validate record tools without Grok Build's costly
  coding-agent context. Preserve ignored tool checkpoints and let the host
  validate, review, and publish. Full completion requires independent semantic and
  editorial review, date repair/fresh re-audit, cross-corpus identity closure and
  a passing master publication. Date inference uses `--lane manual --transport
  grok-build`; identity uses `people:resolve --transport grok-build --run`. Never
  infer corpus identity closure from a sparse chapter checkout. See the lane doc
  for exact sticky calibration ownership and recovery paths; it is not yet
  calibrated production throughput.
- **People extraction budgets and recovery:** `npm run people:extract` defaults new workers to 60 owned units, 150 candidates, and a 48 KiB compact packet, with a $5 / five-million-token per-run circuit breaker. After calibration, the September deadline profile may use 80 units, 200 candidates, the same 48 KiB ceiling, a 20-minute remote timeout, and a three-million-token breaker for fresh chapters only. A run-limit failure affects only that chunk; it must not stop unrelated chapters. An account-level `usage_limit_exceeded` response is different: extraction and editorial schedulers stop launching globally, drain active work, and preserve partial chapters for resumption after capacity returns. When Cursor allowance is at or below 5%, first run a 5-10 chunk calibration cohort, then size the larger wave from accepted p90 usage. Do not put the circuit breaker inside the observed normal completion range or use high concurrency before measuring the remaining allowance. Complete chapters with saved chunks before opening new chapters. `data/people/generated/chunk-extractions/` and `data/people/generated/extraction-state.json` are ignored but economically valuable recovery state: never delete them during cleanup while chapters are incomplete. Resume with `--retry-failed`; validated chunks and adaptive split plans are reused automatically. Retained Cursor conversations are a standard recovery source: the runner continues every interrupted chat before replacing it with a fresh worker. If a continued chat also crosses a run limit, its ownership range is split while all nonoverlapping saved work is preserved. A retained conversation or local accepted/rejected artifact makes a claim sticky; an adaptive chunk plan by itself does not. The scheduler releases never-started claims when a run stops and reconciles orphaned `claimed` reservations on its next startup.
- **People quality-first campaigns:** `data/people/campaign-policy.json` is the single source for lane reset calendars, the rolling planning horizon, and the calibrated wave cap. In September 2026, Grok Bot resumes September 13 and Cursor SDK resumes September 24; never treat those as a shared reset. Forecast rates over the rolling horizon, but never raise the operational cap or weaken validation to satisfy the forecast. Run recovery before fresh work, keep all twelve Grok Bot workers occupied when that lane is available, and calibrate Cursor after its own reset before scaling concurrency. The launcher prioritizes sticky recovery, uses 80-unit/200-candidate/48-KiB packets, and applies calibrated $3 / three-million-token / 20-minute per-run breakers. Invocation ceilings are circuit breakers, not spending targets. Use at least three validation attempts for multi-chunk extraction, independently review translation repairs, and accumulate at least 25 accepted chapters and normally 50 before global identity resolution. Run focused extraction validation after each wave and the full people validator once per reviewed milestone. Push exact checkpoint files to `codex/people-glossary-staging-v2` and merge substantial validated milestones to `master` without triggering a deploy per worker. Optimize duplicated context, abandoned recovery, repeated comparisons, and rebuild overhead; never trade away candidate coverage, evidence, dates, relationships, translation fidelity, or conservative identity decisions for throughput.
- **Reviewed identity ambiguity:** A validated `possible-same-as` decision closes that canonical pair for scheduling while keeping its person records separate. Resolver dossiers expose only the remaining `reviewPairs`, including inside larger same-name blocks, so later waves do not spend capacity reconsidering the same evidence. Replacing either chapter extraction invalidates the affected decision and makes the pair eligible again.
- **Identity candidate pruning:** Use the schema's actual `title-name`, `title-reference`, `regnal-name`, `temple-name`, and `posthumous-name` kinds as non-blocking aliases; reused sovereign titles must not create dynasty-spanning comparison components. Generic kinship labels such as `His Wife` or `其妻` are also non-blocking. When a one-word English reading has a paired Chinese form, do not block on the English reading alone: `Zhong 仲` and `Zhong 忠` remain distinguishable through their Chinese keys, while an exact Chinese mononym can still create a legitimate candidate. Partition a shared Romanized English identity name when every shared English form is supported as an identity name and both records have nonempty, disjoint sets of specific Chinese identity names; preserve the comparison whenever either side lacks that evidence. This removed 10,961 live review pairs and 948 unresolved blocks in the September 9 corpus. Measure resolver load by remaining `reviewPairs`, not raw block count, because partitioning a mixed block can create more small blocks while sharply reducing comparisons.
- **Large identity blocks:** Collapse a well-supported same-person cluster with one transitive multi-person merge instead of emitting every pair. Keep generic surname-clan labels such as `Lady Wang` / `王氏` and exact bare kinship surfaces such as `Wife`, `Third Son`, `Younger Brother`, `妻子`, and `第三子` non-blocking while retaining specific descriptions such as `Wife of Zhang Wenxu`; do not disable the entire descriptive-kinship kind.
- **People generated data:** `catalog.json`, `site-index.json`, and `resolution-candidates.json` are now small atomic manifests backed by generation-scoped shards. Consumers must use `readPeopleCatalog`, `readPeopleSiteIndex`, and `readPeopleResolutionCandidates` from `scripts/lib/people-generated-data.mjs`; direct `readJson` calls only see the manifest. Writers publish the manifest last and remove older generations only after the new one is readable.
- **People editorial review budgets:** Historical accepted reviews have p90 usage near $1.90 and 2.65 million tokens. For the September campaign, use a $3 / four-million-token per-run circuit breaker and a 20-minute remote timeout; the old $1 / one-million-token defaults sit inside normal completion and should not be used for deadline waves. Resume retained reviewer conversations before opening replacements.
- `jq` is a required system tool for `make validate` and scraping targets — it is pre-installed in the VM.
- There is no linter, test suite, or TypeScript — the project has `"test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1"` in `package.json`.
- **`make update BOOK=<book>`** is the usual incremental build after editing one book; **`make update-all`** rebuilds the whole site. Both regenerate static HTML and OG assets as appropriate and sync to `public/`. If `data/manifest.json` is missing, `make update` runs a full `make manifest` first. `data/manifest.json`, `data/progress.json`, and their `public/data/` copies are gitignored (regenerated by `make manifest` / `make progress` / `npm run build`).
- Scraping targets (`make shiji-001`, etc.) require internet access to chinesenotes.com/ctext.org and are interactive (prompt before overwriting translated chapters).
- `package-lock.json` is gitignored, so `npm install` resolves latest compatible versions each time.
### OpenRouter free fallback lane

Use `OPENROUTER_PEOPLE_LANE.md` for the local zero-priced OpenRouter extraction and independent date-audit runners. The same stable worker ID resumes sticky work; never delete ignored OpenRouter response/chunk files or date-workflow recovery state during disk cleanup. The free tier is request-limited and upstream models can return 429; stop and resume later, without silently switching to paid models or weakening validators. The extraction runner marks validated chapters `ready` but does not publish them; the host orchestrator remains responsible for exact-file staging and normal review gates. One shared checkout suffices.

### Verified ebook people glossaries

Follow `PEOPLE_EBOOK_CERTIFICATION.md` for required-glossary ebook generation.
A complete book or manifest-defined volume can qualify independently of unrelated
histories while retaining current global identity decisions. The ordinary compiler
seal and current extraction, editorial, independent date and identity gates remain
mandatory. Preview output does not satisfy certification.
files.PEOPLE_COMPLETION_PROCESS.md:
# Completion-first people glossary process

This is the current orchestration policy.

**October 30, 2026 user-authorized process revision:** chapter completion uses
bounded canonical-person dossier reviews, not exhaustive O(k²) same-name pair
comparisons. This explicitly supersedes the old zero-touching-pairs completion
condition. Adoption still requires integrated code, independent review, passing
CI and a real nonempty live chapter receipt; this text alone grants no approval. It supersedes extraction-volume targets,
old deadline wave recipes, and waiting for 25–50 new extractions before identity work.
Existing source, editorial, chronology, identity and publication gates remain intact.
A planning checkpoint grants no approval.

## First prove a real delivery

Continue the existing owner/work for Jinshu 053 as the first nonempty pilot. If held,
record the precise obstacle and choose the next already-extracted Jinshu chapter with
the smallest total downstream workload. Do not choose an empty extraction to satisfy
this milestone, or re-extract to avoid a downstream gate. No new broad extraction
wave until a nonempty chapter is verified live. Drain/recover existing claims rather
than abandoning them. Use one shared checkout and isolated artifact paths; this policy
does not authorize a second executor or taking over an active chapter.


## Repair English omissions when found

A definite English omission or mistranslation requires a concrete complete replacement,
not only a flag or an outside-scope note. Check both English fields and repeated uses.
Supply supplemental repairs in an artifact with book, chapter, unit ID, field, exact
before/after text and source-based reason; keep them separate from closed-schema date
or identity reports. The host routes these into the active editorial application work,
with a separate reviewer for worker-authored repairs. Preserve independent review and
normal extraction, chronology, identity, CI and publication gates. Do not defer known
fixable English to a future corpus-wide pass. An empty proposal queue alone does not
prove every source proposition has been translated.

## Bounded chapter work order

1. Finish source/editorial corrections first: paired translations, repeated names and
   transcription. Run current extraction/editorial gates. Repair the existing extraction;
   re-extract only for a demonstrated defect that requires it.
2. Obtain current independent date approval. Genuinely undated facts stay undated;
   actual ambiguity stays on research hold. Follow the date loop breaker, not repeated
   whole-chapter reviews of unchanged candidates.
3. Pin the actual source, extraction, editorial history and date-report bytes. Record
   a small work order under `data/people/generated/completion/BOOK/NNN/`, not a checkout.
   Keep the original evidence in place; a fingerprint is not permission to rewrite it.
4. Reuse the current immutable canonical-person dossier registry. Build/update it
   once from validated source records and accepted membership decisions, never once
   per review packet. One logical dossier represents one accepted canonical person;
   chapter records remain its cited provenance. Historical merge, separation and
   reviewed-ambiguity decisions remain valid constraints, not a new all-pairs queue.
5. Prepare one case per canonical person occurring in this chapter, covering every
   chapter-local record exactly once. Retrieve at most eight other dossiers per
   case through the name/alias index, with at most sixteen keys and eight posting
   reads per key. Record full posting counts/fingerprints, every omitted key and
   every overflow. Retrieval limits are admission limits, never proof of uniqueness
   or permission to discard a plausible match. No complete same-name pair graph,
   connected-component completion, or recursive external-chapter completion.
6. Independently review each case's source-backed retained identity assignment and
   exact cited Chinese evidence. The reviewer must confirm that the record denotes
   an actual individual, its chapter mentions belong to that record, and the accepted
   canonical membership is supported. An unresolved cross-chapter equivalence may
   finish as explicit reviewed uncertainty while records remain separate. It must
   not create a confident separation, a guessed match, or a new merge. A suspected
   false existing merge, unsupported chapter-person attribution, or conflicting
   primary evidence remains a concrete case hold. New merges still use the existing
   independently reviewed resolution-application gates.
7. Once every chapter-local person has current independent case coverage and no
   concrete case hold, run actual scoped website qualification/projection. A legacy
   same-name candidate count is not the chapter's release gate. Publication must
   preserve reviewed cross-chapter uncertainty visibly and reconstruct facts only
   from qualified source members. Source/extraction/editorial/date, unsupported
   family-target, source-fidelity, quote/artifact, CI and live-content gates remain.
   Do not use preview flags or change stale approval hashes to obtain a green result.

Freezing inputs means no speculative cleanup during downstream review, not ignoring
factual errors. Independently review genuine corrections, preserve the old generation,
reconcile affected work, and obtain fresh affected approvals. Do not change hashes to
keep approvals. Keep unrelated extraction changes out of the pilot acceptance release.

## Historical pair checkpoints and spending stops

The following retained command compares historical pair-frontier receipts. It is
diagnostic recovery tooling; its pair count is no longer a release gate or a model
worklist. New dossier checkpoints report person cases, approved/held cases, reviewed
uncertainty, source input pins, reviewer receipts and publication evidence.

Compare two historical compact checkpoints with:

```sh
npm run people:completion:check -- --baseline /absolute/baseline.json --current /absolute/current.json
```

Each JSON contains `scope: {book, chapter}`, chapter-local extracted `personCount`, `inputs` containing
SHA-256 byte digests for `source`, `extraction`, `editorial`, `dateAudit`, and
`unresolvedPairs`, an array of distinct two-element canonical-ID pairs. Derive pairs
from the current validated graph, not model estimates/raw block counts. Record graph
revision/generation and accepted decision receipts beside each checkpoint. Hash file
bytes, not paths. Do not substitute checkpoints for sealed evidence.

The command is read-only and diagnostic: it does not validate decisions, graph
freshness, date reports or publication. Input/people-count drift or added pair IDs
returns `replan-required` and nonzero exit. Zero pairs means `ready-for-release-checks`,
never `complete`. Zero-person checkpoints return `empty-scope` with nonzero exit;
they cannot satisfy the nonempty pilot. Malformed
checkpoints fail loudly. Preserve sequential checkpoints to expose reversals.

Date work permits at most three automatic repair/re-audit rounds and stops earlier
for repeated candidates or two non-improving rounds (`PEOPLE_DATE_AUDIT.md`). For
identity work, repeated unchanged case/evidence fingerprints require diagnosis
before another model turn. Reuse unchanged independent case proofs; reconcile
source edits and accepted membership changes explicitly. Do not
delete state, release sticky work, raise limits or change worker IDs to bypass a hold.
Continue another bounded chapter if useful work cannot proceed. A hold is neither a
completion nor a campaign-wide stop.

## What counts as done

Report these separately:

- Extracted/repaired: intermediate work, not glossary completion.
- Data-qualified nonempty chapter: current source/editorial/date/identity gates pass.
- Verified zero-person chapter: reviewed extraction contains no people; no pages
  expected. This does not prove the nonempty pipeline. Genre alone does not prove
  absence of people: check source review and candidate coverage.
- Published nonempty chapter: qualified output merged/deployed, generated person
  pages, both-language chapter links, inverse snippets, search and sitemap targets
  pass site verifiers and live HTTP/content checks for that deployment.

The first acceptance receipt must identify the chapter, nonzero published people,
exact source/approval/identity inputs, merged revision, successful deployment,
generated verification results and live checked person/chapter/search/sitemap URLs.
Check multiple mentions, shared names and inverse links; a 200 fallback page does
not pass. Check slug redirects where applicable. Changed inputs invalidate a stale
receipt. Synthetic fixtures are regression tests, not this production receipt.

Do not report published completion from claims, unit tests, PRs, audit approval,
build success alone or an empty extraction. Do not wait for 30 other chapters before
releasing the first nonempty acceptance slice: this is an exception to batch-size
targets, not to CI/master rules. Use exact reviewed changes and the normal PR path.

## Scale only the demonstrated path

### Crash-recovery operating profile (October 26, 2026)

The last crash was preceded by measured Codex backend allocations of about 79 GiB
and roughly 55 GiB swapped out; free disk subsequently fell below 1 GiB. A local
graph pass peaked around 2.4 GiB of JavaScript heap. These observations identify a
backend memory problem as a major contributor; they do not establish its software
cause. Do not assume free disk, cloud inference, compaction or simply reopening the
same long chat fixes it.

Use this conservative profile until successful small runs justify changes:

This host-safety profile overrides historical lane-filling and concurrency targets.
Let already-running assignments drain; retained or ready claims are not permission
to launch more work and must not be released merely to reduce concurrency.

- Use a fresh coordination chat with only a compact work-order handoff and exact
  evidence/receipt paths. Do not fork this campaign's accumulated history. End at
  the first bounded batch checkpoint or 60 minutes, whichever comes first; preserve
  a handoff before rotating. This is a session boundary, not permission to discard
  work, abandon sticky conversations or weaken any acceptance gate.
- Do not resume an unbounded automatic goal loop in the old chat. This crash-policy
  repair is the final task here; glossary production resumes from the saved handoff
  in a fresh chat. Do not create a recurring automation as a workaround.
- Initially use no parallel native Codex subagents. Independent author/reviewer
  conversations remain separate but run sequentially, with bounded sealed evidence
  rather than inherited full campaign history. Start with one cloud assignment.
  Consider two only after two completed assignments and their host acceptance checks
  show stable resources. This does not authorize more spend or new extraction.
- Run only one local heavy job at a time. Do not overlap full graph compilation,
  site/ebook builds, Git packing, or large packet construction. Use a 3 GiB Node
  old-space ceiling for newly launched heavy Node jobs; this limits JavaScript heap,
  not native buffers or total RSS. If it fails, preserve the partial run and change
  the batching/streaming approach rather than repeatedly raising the ceiling.
- Run `npm run people:disk:check` before each new dispatch/heavy job, after a job,
  and at least every 60 seconds while observing active work. On macOS it checks disk,
  system swap, Codex backend resident memory and OS memory pressure. Keep 30 GiB
  free; warn at 4 GiB swap and inspect consumers and growth before increasing
  concurrency. Stop new work at 8 GiB swap, 4 GiB combined Codex backend RSS, or warning/
  critical memory pressure. Unknown/failed measurements fail closed. Other platforms
  explicitly report this macOS memory check as not applicable, not as verified safe.
- These are admission checks, not a continuous watchdog or an application memory
  limit. On a breach, stop new dispatches, checkpoint compact state and end the
  coordination turn. Preserve current job IDs and verify actual remote/process
  state before resuming. Never auto-kill the user's Codex/browser, delete swap,
  clear history, remove locks or discard recovery. If growth continues, ask the user
  to quit the app; a repository script cannot safely repair its allocator.
- Bound tool output: normally return at most 1,000 tokens, at most 4,000 for a
  necessary code review. Save large logs/results to their existing job artifacts;
  return counts, hashes and paths. Project search/connector responses before printing
  them. Never dump a corpus, entire API response, huge diff, or long conversation.
- Recover known cloud agents by stable ID. Scan historical agents only for an
  actual missing-ID recovery, not every poll or fresh assignment. Save agent/run IDs,
  usage and output paths as soon as available. Reuse sealed graph/results on unchanged
  inputs; refresh once per reviewed data/semantic change, not per polling turn.

Do not claim this repairs a Codex backend leak or guarantees crash prevention.
It limits exposure and stops new work well before the previously observed failure.
Keep the existing shared date-audit pool, worker IDs, packet ceilings, validation,
review independence and publication gates; do not introduce competing executors.

After the first live receipt, use a bounded WIP cohort (initially at most three
chapters), prioritizing Jinshu and ranking total remaining completion work. Spend
lanes on disjoint downstream packets, not competing host executors. Size later waves
from accepted published-chapter cost/time and failure rates, not tokens consumed or
extraction throughput. Leave capacity unused rather than repeat an unchanged hold.

Ship qualified cohorts incrementally. At book completion, generate/verify the
certified ebook glossary against the authoritative full book/volume manifest.
One published chapter does not make the whole Jinshu ebook release-ready.

## Adoption by the running orchestrator

Let active invocations drain. Preserve locks, leases, conversations and sealed inputs.
At an idle boundary adopt reviewed code/policy, record the existing pilot owner, and
initialize its work order from latest accepted inputs/current graph. Do not reset
Jinshu 053 or repeat passed checks on unchanged inputs merely to adopt this policy.
Reuse gate fixes already on master instead of rebuilding them from an older host
checkout. Documenting policy is not proof the running orchestrator adopted it: report
adoption, data qualification and live publication separately.

# Bounded chapter completion

The operational deliverable is a deployed nonempty chapter with current source,
editorial, chronology, identity, backlinks, search, sitemap and ebook-contribution
checks. Completed packets and reduced pair counters are intermediate work.

## The necessary rule change

A chapter certifies its source-backed person records and their accepted identity
assignments. It does not certify that every similarly named person elsewhere has
been ruled out. Cross-chapter equivalence may remain explicitly uncertain after
independent source review. A genuine false merge or uncertain attribution inside
this chapter is a hold; a broad name index is not.

The old zero-touching-pairs gate must be replaced, not renamed or secretly set to
zero. Historical pair decisions remain constraints and evidence. Their unresolved
backlog remains historical research debt, separately reported. No workflow may
create a complete same-name pair graph to generate matching or publication work.

## One dossier and one reviewed case

1. Maintain an immutable, versioned dossier per accepted canonical person. Preserve
   every local member, source-backed name/alias, claim reference and membership
   proof. The dossier is identity-review evidence, not permission to publish facts
   from unqualified external chapters.
2. Maintain an inverted name/alias index over dossiers. Build/update the registry
   once per accepted source delta. Load it once and reuse it across chapter jobs;
   do not compile the global graph per worker, packet, poll or minor correction.
3. For each canonical person in the chapter, retrieve at most eight other dossiers.
   Read at most sixteen name keys and eight postings per key. Prefer specific
   Chinese names, then full English names. Keep Chinese variant handling and the
   existing source-backed generic-title rules. A ranking is retrieval, never a
   factual identity verdict.
4. Retain complete key counts/fingerprints and explicit overflow. An oversized
   bucket produces an ambiguity review, not hundreds of pair assignments. The
   reviewer reads the chapter's identity evidence and the relevant dossier evidence,
   approves the retained source identity or holds a concrete contradiction. No
   uninspected remainder is labelled different-person, reviewed, or impossible.
5. Only positive source-backed identification may propose a merge. A new merge
   still needs separate independent review and normal native application. Lack of
   a match leaves a separate record with honest uncertainty, not a guessed merge.
6. Store the actual independent report, source witnesses, plan and input hashes.
   A certificate covers every local person exactly once and is checked against
   current source/extraction/editorial/date bytes. It cannot itself merge, split,
   retract a known constraint, or grant source/date/publication approval.

Index construction is linear in input evidence plus sorting posting lists. Chapter
preparation is O(Ap + Mp + p × q × r), with Ap aliases and Mp protected members in the chapter dossiers, p chapter people, q <= 16 posting keys and r <= 8 reads.
The source context still takes time proportional to the evidence that must be read.
There is no k × k loop for a k-person same-name bucket. At most eight candidate
headers enter a case; zero unordered pair assignments are generated.

## Retain useful completed work

A source identity edit invalidates the affected proof. Unrelated chapters, a new
name posting, or another accepted source for an existing person must not reopen
all earlier reviewed people. Retain old reports unchanged. Reconcile accepted merge
lineage/redirects mechanically and verify each proof's actual source dependencies.
Current chapter byte pins, fresh required chronology approvals and exact primary
witnesses are still checked. Never change approval hashes to preserve approval.

The prototype already permits accepted canonical membership growth without
reopening unchanged chapter-local identity evidence. Source-identity edits, new
chapter people, stale chapter inputs and unknown reviewer/merge fields fail closed.
Further selective reuse after an editorial edit must be implemented as an auditable
new aggregate over unchanged individual proofs, not by rewriting an old report.

## Target an ordinary chapter in about one hour

| Elapsed time | Deliverable |
| --- | --- |
| 0–10 minutes | Validate current extraction and source/editorial/date gates; reuse unchanged passed work. |
| 10–30 minutes | Bounded dossier preparation and independent identity review; apply only independently proven merges. |
| 30–45 minutes | Qualification, both-language mentions, inverse excerpts, website/search/sitemap and ebook contribution checks. |
| 45–60 minutes | Clean release PR, required CI/build, merge/deploy, live content checks and the nonempty acceptance receipt. |

These are time budgets to measure, not permission to approve missing evidence.
Jinshu053 already has source/editorial and current independent date pins, so those
passed stages should be reused. A chapter requiring genuine historical research
gets an exact source issue/hold; we do not launch repeated unchanged review rounds.
Unknown dates may remain unknown only through the existing chronology representation
and independent approval, never by inventing years or disguising an audit hold.

Keep one completion WIP chapter until the first nonempty release is verified.
After that, admit at most three, sized from measured completed/published throughput.
Retain current ownership, all recovery, one shared checkout and the host resource
profile. No new extraction campaign while this acceptance path is unproven.

## Production integration is part of acceptance

The new engine is not active merely because its tests pass. Before claiming the
one-hour path works:

- Replace fresh work generation in the existing resolver with dossier cases. Old
  unfinished assignments retain recovery; no fresh quadratic pair wave is sent.
- Persist and load the registry by immutable manifest; verify retrieved bytes.
- Consume independent per-person review proofs in the shared qualified-scope gate.
  Remove the global all-pairs veto from chapter qualification. Keep actual source,
  editorial, date, family, artifact, quotation, coverage and CI checks intact.
- Revalidate proof dependencies and accepted canonical lineage without forcing a
  whole-corpus reread or reopening unchanged cases.
- Display reviewed identity uncertainty; do not present provisional records as
  confident distinct historical individuals or silently suppress their mentions.
- Prove real Jinshu053 coverage, generate normal outputs, pass CI, deploy and check
  their actual content. Report reviewed cases, held cases, ambiguous identities,
  data-qualified chapters and live published nonempty chapters separately.

Current state: compact accepted-constraint replay, immutable dossiers and bounded
planning are implemented. Candidate scheduler entry points refuse fresh pair waves;
the shared qualification gate and website/ebook uncertainty disclosure have candidate
integration code. Jinshu053 has a native-accepted independent report covering all
72 cases/73 local records (63 reviewed uncertain), with exact unchanged input pins.
Code adoption, remaining CI fixture/command integration, a passing normal build,
PR/deployment and live nonempty receipt are still required. No chapter is published
or data-qualified by this checkpoint. The one-hour release target remains unproven.

{
  "name": "records-of-the-grand-historian",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "scrape.js",
  "scripts": {
    "people:disk:check": "node scripts/check-local-disk.mjs",
    "people:disk:self-test": "node --test scripts/test-local-disk.mjs",
    "test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1",
    "build": "node scripts/assert-people-production-build.mjs && node scripts/test-people-production-build.mjs && node scripts/test-site-urls.mjs && node scripts/test-kindle-availability.mjs && node scripts/sync-publication-descriptions.mjs && node scripts/sync-data-to-public.mjs && node generate-manifest.js && node scripts/compile-people-catalog.mjs && node scripts/test-people-progress.mjs && node scripts/scan-placeholder-translations.mjs --out data/quality/placeholder-translations.json --summary --limit=0 && node generate-progress.js && node scripts/generate-book-covers.mjs && node generate-static-pages.js && node scripts/generate-people-pages.mjs && node scripts/verify-people-site.mjs && node scripts/build-book-search-corpus.mjs && node scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs && node generate-og-images.js --incremental && node scripts/verify-og-assets.mjs",
    "people:production-build:self-test": "node scripts/test-people-production-build.mjs",
    "test:site-urls": "node scripts/test-site-urls.mjs",
    "test:kindle-availability": "node scripts/test-kindle-availability.mjs",
    "test:people-progress": "node scripts/test-people-progress.mjs",
    "publication-descriptions": "node scripts/sync-publication-descriptions.mjs",
    "publication-descriptions:init": "node scripts/sync-publication-descriptions.mjs --init-md-from-json",
    "publication-descriptions:check": "node scripts/sync-publication-descriptions.mjs --check",
    "people:normalize-ids": "node scripts/normalize-content-unit-ids.mjs --apply",
    "people:check-ids": "node scripts/normalize-content-unit-ids.mjs --check",
    "people:normalize-ids:self-test": "node scripts/normalize-content-unit-ids.mjs --self-test",
    "people:hints:normalize": "node scripts/normalize-people-date-hints.mjs",
    "people:hints:self-test": "node --test scripts/test-people-date-hints.mjs scripts/test-people-date-hints-validator-cli.mjs",
    "people:packet": "node scripts/build-people-extraction-packet.mjs",
    "people:packet:self-test": "node scripts/build-people-extraction-packet.mjs --self-test",
    "people:chunks:self-test": "node scripts/test-people-extraction-chunks.mjs",
    "people:compile-extraction": "node scripts/compile-people-extraction.mjs",

findings.reason: The live compile path does use resolveAcceptedPeopleClusters plus assessCorpusIdentityReviews (generatedPairs 0; identityReviewByChapter; no unresolvedCanonicalPeople pair veto). The same file's selfTest still asserts resolutionWorkByChapter, unresolvedCandidateBlocks, and writeCompiledPeopleOutputs writers catalog,candidates,siteIndex. people:catalog:self-test would not prove the new catalog and currently encodes the retired pair/candidates contract. Migrate that self-test (and other CI fixtures named in knownRemainingWork) to identityReviewByChapter / identityReviewPendingChapters / seal v2 before treating compiler regression as green. Do not restore pair expansion to make the old assertions pass.

HTML overview can emit IDENTITY_UNCERTAINTY_NOTE, but personOverview, personJsonLd description/alternateName, and search cards still present the record as an ordinary distinct Person with no uncertainty. Policy requires not presenting reviewed-ambiguous identities as confident distinct historical individuals. Carry the same note into JSON-LD and the public search snippet, or equivalent visible machine-readable uncertainty, before calling website/ebook presentation complete. Ebook HTML already has the glossary note; this gap is the person-page structured data/lede.

Evidence/anchor chapters load with strictAliasDispositions:false. Native extraction validation still runs, and facts are not taken from those chapters, but alias-disposition failures there will not fail the chapter gate. Confirm that identity keys/witnesses cannot change under that looser flag, or require the same strict alias contract used for the target chapter.

resolveAcceptedPeopleClusters matches the native constraint measurement (258210 locals, exact membership/lineage, generatedPairs 0, 3000-trial semanticsMatch). resolvePeopleClusters still Cartesian-expands keep-separate/possible-same-as for historical drain and remains imported by the compiler even though compilePeopleCatalog does not call it. Keep it off the catalog/qualification/prepare path; deadline resolution already refuses fresh waves. Verify leftover callers are drain-only.

Still says scheduler/gate/rendering integration and a real independent chapter review are required and that no chapter was made complete. The candidate now has those hooks plus a 72-case/73-person native-accepted report. Leave the non-adoption caveats; update the prototype-state paragraph so operators do not think the pair veto is still the live chapter gate in this candidate, and do not treat that report as data-qualified or published (productionCodeAdopted/dataQualified/published remain false).

priorFindings.reason: This is not a published or data-qualified chapter and not an adoption approval. Shared qualification now independently revalidates each retained dossier proof against current primary units and person-dependency fingerprints, reconstructs facts only from scoped validated members, keeps source/date/editorial/family gates, and stamps reviewed uncertainty onto catalog/ebook HTML. Compact constraint replay measured equivalent to prior membership/lineage with generatedPairs 0; Jinshu 053 72/73 native proof is a sealed review receipt, not a live site. Mention-span witnesses accept validated abbreviations/kinship (衍長女/長女) and still reject unrelated Han (美, 字) and invented people. Changes are required before calling the candidate CI/presentation-complete: the compiler's own self-test still demands pair-era catalog fields/candidate writers, and person-page JSON-LD/search/lede omit the uncertainty the HTML note is supposed to enforce. Remaining listed work (CI fixture migration, registry builder, scheduler automation, deployment, selective proof reuse after edits) stays unfinished and must not be counted as a green release.
